newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone war orphans find $500,000 diamond.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone war orphans find $500,000 diamond.

text.p: Three hungry war orphans digging for wild yams in the impoverished West African nation of Sierra Leone stumbled on a flawless 100 carat diamond worth at least $500,000, officials said on Wednesday.

The orphans, whose parents were killed in a rebel attack on their village of Hinnah Malen in the southern Pujehun district two years ago, found the diamond nestling under a yam near the village on Tuesday.
Morie Jah, 14, the oldest boy, told reporters they had gone out early after two days without food but decided to return home hungry after searching in vain for yams for three hours.
"On the way back we found a yam under a palm tree and dug it up. Right under the yam we found the diamond. It was easy to see because it was shining and sparkling," he said.
Valuers at the government gold and diamond office in the capital Freetown said the stone was worth at least $500,000.

It was not immediately clear how much money the children, who were returned to the village last week for the first time since the attack that killed their parents, would get from the sale of the stone.

President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who took office last March after multi-party elections ended four years of military rule, has struck a peace deal with rebels who took up arms in 1991. Implementation details are still being worked out.
